message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to live data feeds, so I can’t tell you the current air‑quality index (AQI) for Los Angeles right now.  

If you’d like up‑to‑date information, you can check one of the following:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the latest AQI and pollutant breakdown. |
| **OpenAQ** | Use their API or website (https://openaq.org/) to pull recent measurements from local monitoring stations. |
| **Weather apps** | Many weather services (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or smartphone weather widgets) display AQI values for major cities. |
| **Local news** | TV or online news outlets often report on smog alerts when AQI exceeds certain thresholds. |

If you’re interested in historical trends or want to analyze how LA’s air quality has changed over time, let me know—I can help you find datasets or explain how to interpret them!
